findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Inline into the plan body (not just a ticket comment) the complete named-hook vocabulary (each pre/post hook's name, contract, and ordering) and the pins callable-evaluation protocol, co-located with the ToolSpec field definitions.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'pre (gate hooks), post (result hooks)'
Plan Approach: 'The named hooks, pins, the eight input overrides, and the ten declared divergences carried verbatim from the manifest are itemised in this ticket's first comment.'

The factory 'runs the PRE hooks ... runs the POST hooks in order' but the plan body never enumerates which hooks exist, their signatures/contract, or how pins callables are evaluated — these are the processing protocol the executor needs to build the 48 derived tools' input/behavior.
findings.finding: The pre/post hook vocabulary and the pins callable protocol — the per-call decision rules the derive_tool factory runs — are referenced by the ToolSpec schema but their definitions are deferred out of the plan body into 'this ticket's first comment', so the schema and the protocol that consumes it are not co-located in the reviewable material.
findings.location: Approach section ('ToolSpec is a frozen dataclass: ... pre (gate hooks), post (result hooks)' and 'The named hooks, pins, the eight input overrides, and the ten declared divergences ... are itemised in this ticket's first comment')
scenarios: An executor builds _mcp_derive.py and _mcp_tool_specs.py but cannot know the full set of hooks, their call contract, or pin-callable evaluation semantics without the deferred comment, risking an inputSchema/behavior divergence the golden test alone may not catch for order/pins.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (with a cite to the installed mcp.server.fastmcp func_metadata path) that FastMCP's schema generation honors the wrapper's injected __signature__/__annotations__ through all four composed decorator layers, and justify hand-rolling parameter stripping instead of the SDK's native func_metadata skip_names facility.
evidence: Plan: 'creates ONE wrapper def tool(*args, **kwargs) that sig.binds ... sets __name__, __doc__, __signature__, __annotations__; then registers with mcp.tool(...)'
Plan: 'functools.wraps propagates __signature__ through them'

Retrieved (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk issue 226): 'python-sdk/src/mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py def func_metadata(func, skip_names=()) -> ... pydantic model representing its signature' — the SDK derives schema from signature introspection and offers skip_names for parameter dropping
Retrieved (gofastmcp.com/servers/tools): FastMCP 'converts Python functions into MCP tools by inspecting the function’s signature and type annotations'

Installed SDK is mcp.server.fastmcp (resolve_symbol origin .venv/.../mcp/server/fastmcp/__init__.py), i.e. the SDK-bundled FastMCP, so standalone FastMCP v3 Tool.from_tool() transformation prior art is NOT available as an alternative here
findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing assertion — that FastMCP's schema generation will read the wrapper's injected __signature__/__annotations__ (set after sig.bind on a `def tool(*args, **kwargs)` body) rather than the wrapper's real variadic signature — is asserted but not grounded against the installed SDK's actual introspection path (mcp.server.fastmcp.utilities.func_metadata.func_metadata, which builds the pydantic schema model and already provides a native `skip_names` facility for dropping parameters).
findings.location: Approach section ("creates ONE wrapper def tool(*args, **kwargs) ... sets __signature__ ... functools.wraps propagates __signature__ through them")
scenarios: If func_metadata introspects the raw wrapper before __signature__ is honored, every derived tool would expose an (*args, **kwargs) schema and the golden test would catch it only after the whole derivation is built
If the SDK's own skip_names could strip repo_root/_private params more robustly than a hand-rolled Signature rebuild, the factory reinvents an available facility

findings.finding: The acceptance criterion asserts `grep -c "@mcp.tool" src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` reports 8 and 1 (=9 total), but the plan elsewhere states 16 `mcp_only` tools 'remain hand-written in their registrars'. scenarios: Executor greps and sees 9, expects 16, cannot tell if the derivation accidentally removed hand-written tools or whether the count is correct by design

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the positive rationale for choosing the factory + override-table (structural single-source guarantee: the input shape CANNOT diverge from the library signature) over the lighter alternative of keeping the hand-copied closures guarded only by the committed golden test, and explain why that structural guarantee justifies superseding topaz-blubbery-mice's Pattern-A rejection for MCP.
evidence: Epic c996-8a5f-5123-4f8e: 'We deliberately do NOT generate the surfaces (Pattern A): behavior is already single-sourced ... and the adapters carry irreducible hand-written value (MCP LLM-facing docstrings, CLI ergonomics), so regenerating them would risk agent/user-visible contract breaks.'

Plan Approach: ToolSpec carries 'description (verbatim ...), ... params ..., order, pins ..., pre ..., post ...' — i.e. the override table re-encodes the hand-written value the epic called irreducible.
The committed golden test (test_live_surface_equals_golden over 64 tools) is itself a complete shape/description/annotations drift tripwire, independent of the factory.
ABSENCE: the plan gives the problem and the mechanism but no sentence answering 'why generation+table rather than keep the closures + the golden test we are already adding?'
findings.finding: The plan reverses a prior ADR decision (topaz-blubbery-mice explicitly 'deliberately do NOT generate the surfaces (Pattern A)' because the adapters carry 'irreducible hand-written value') and simultaneously commits a byte-level golden test, but states no positive rationale for why the ~750-LOC factory + override-table (which re-encodes that 'irreducible' value as verbatim descriptions/params/order/pins/hooks) is worth adopting OVER the golden test alone as the drift guard.
findings.location: Approach section; Context/Problem ('ADR 0119 supersedes that clause for MCP only'); Testing (golden)
scenarios: An implementer or future reader weighing whether the factory earns its complexity and ADR reversal has no stated rationale to rely on
A later reviewer re-litigates the Pattern A rejection because the superseding rationale is implicit
findings.suggested_fix: Add one or two sentences to the Approach: e.g. 'A golden test alone is only a post-hoc tripwire — shape can still drift and is caught after the fact; deriving the input signature from the single library parameter list makes shape divergence structurally impossible, which is why 0119 supersedes the Pattern-A clause for MCP while the override table still carries the verbatim LLM-facing descriptions the epic flagged as irreducible.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback for the hint-resolution sub-step (e.g. fail fast naming the unresolved symbol and requiring a params override, or an explicit localns extension point) when typing.get_type_hints cannot resolve a parameter.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'resolves hints with typing.get_type_hints(... localns=vars(rebar.types)) (never inspect.signature(eval_str=True), which raises on the TYPE_CHECKING-only TypedDict names)'

ABSENCE: the plan prescribes the happy-path resolution but no behavior for a hint that is still unresolvable under the chosen globalns/localns (e.g. a newly introduced name not in rebar.types), i.e. an unspecified fallback for a failed derivation sub-step.
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for the derivation sub-step where typing.get_type_hints cannot resolve a parameter hint; the plan notes the prior inspect.signature(eval_str=True) approach 'raises on the TYPE_CHECKING-only TypedDict names' but does not state what derive_tool does if get_type_hints itself fails for a given library symbol.
findings.location: Approach section ('resolves hints with typing.get_type_hints(fn, globalns=..., localns=vars(rebar.types)) (never inspect.signature(eval_str=True), which raises ...)')
scenarios: A library signature later adds a parameter annotated with a name not reachable via vars(sys.modules[fn.__module__]) or vars(rebar.types); derive_tool's get_type_hints raises at import/registration with no declared handling, taking down server startup rather than producing an actionable error.
